sampling_method: This is the CVPR two-column layout with a 15-page appendix (30 pages in all). Reading order is page order and, within a page, the left column in full and then the right column in full; a float is read at the top of the column it occupies, before the body text below it, and a float that spans the full page width (Table 2, Figures 8, 9 and 18) is read before both columns of that page. Two places where that convention decides something: on page 10 Table 3 sits in the left column and Table 4 at the top of the right column, so all of Table 3 precedes all of Table 4; and on page 11 Table 5 precedes Figure 11, both in the left column, while the Section 7.6 text that follows them is in the right column. Table 2, Table 6 and Table 8 are each printed as side-by-side blocks under one caption and are read block by block, left block first, rows top-to-bottom and, within a row, left-to-right across its own-result columns only. Figure 18's four-entry legends are read as printed, left-to-right then top-to-bottom, i.e. RITM, SAM, SAM - single output, GT. The appendix sits where it is printed: after the references (pages 13-15, which carry nothing), so appendix cells occupy the tail of the population, indices 100-159, and no main-text cell is displaced by it. Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 1-based index in that order, giving a population of 1..159. Ownership was settled per cell, from citation brackets first and from stated provenance where a bracket conflicts with the text. Tables 2 and 6 (SAM's performance segmenting people and clothing) contain no baseline at all -- every row is SAM -- so ownership there is not a judgement call, and the same is true of Figures 9a, 11 and 18 and of Table 8, where the numbers reported are the authors' own measurements even where what was measured belongs to someone else: the ratings of RITM's and ViTDet-H's masks, and of the LVIS and COCO ground truth, were all produced by this paper's human study, which is the ConvNeXt case of a caption claiming the measurement while the method stays quoted. Table 4's ViTDet-H [62] row is counted as an own result on the strength of Appendix D.3, which describes the authors rerunning and modifying cascade ViTDet-H to emit 1000 proposals -- the authors' own rerun of a prior model is an own result. Table 5's ViTDet-H [62] row is the one place where the evidence genuinely conflicts: the row carries a citation, yet Appendix D.4 says the authors ran a fully-supervised ViTDet-H on both validation splits for the box prompts and Appendix E says they rated its masks, so the AP values may be their measurement or may be quoted. The row is kept in the frame and the one cell the sample drew from it (frame_index 83) is recorded with confident: false rather than guessed. Table 3's uncited 'Sobel filter, 1968, .539' row is excluded as a baseline: the Results prose attributes that whole block to 'prior, though admittedly outdated, zero-shot transfer methods', its two companions in the block are cited, and the paper never claims to have run the operator. Counting it would make Table 3 5 and N 160. Excluded as dataset_statistic, which is what keeps this paper's frame small relative to its length: the SA-1B size figures wherever they appear (abstract, Figures 1, 2 and 6, Sections 1, 4 and 5, the Dataset Card) -- 11M images, 1.1B masks, ~100 masks per image, 99.1% automatic, 3300x4950 resolution; all 48 cells of Table 1, which reports how many countries, images and masks fall in each region and income band for SA-1B, COCO and Open Images; and all 46 '# images sampled' / '# masks sampled' cells of Table 7. Excluded as hyperparameter: the whole of Appendix A's architecture and training recipe, Appendix B's pipeline thresholds, and Appendix D's evaluation protocol. The line drawn between the two roles and 'result' is that a number describing what the dataset or the configuration contains is not a result, while a number describing how well something performed -- mIoU, AP, AR, ODS/OIS/R50, a human mask-quality rating, a p-value, a runtime, an annotation time, an error rate, a training cost -- is. That line is what admits the 34/14/34-second annotation times, the 90-second rating time, the 0.83 rater standard deviation, the two 4% postprocessing error rates and the Model Card's 68 hours / 6963 kWh / 2.8 metric tons, and it is the judgement in this file a reviewer is most likely to want to check. Deltas: the paper prints few, and the rule cuts both ways. Figure 9a's 23 signed per-dataset deltas count, because no absolute per-dataset mIoU is printed anywhere in the paper; Section 7.1's '~47 IoU' counts as a fresh printed instance at a new location; Section 7.6's '~0.5 mIoU' counts because Figure 13, where its absolutes would live, prints only axis ticks. Against that, '6.5x faster than mask annotation for COCO' and '2x slower than bounding-box labeling' are not counted because the absolute 14 seconds is printed in the same breath, and the Model Card's '~7k miles driven' is not counted because it is the 2.8 metric tons restated in equivalent units in the same breath. Not counted as cells for other reasons: ranges and intervals -- 'inter-annotator consistency at 85-91% IoU' (also a citation), 'ratings fall between 7 and 9', '94-108 masks per image', and all 16 CI99 columns of Table 8, which print pairs such as '(1.40, 1.84)'; the bound 'less than 1% of the image encoder's compute'; and the tally '16 of the 23 datasets', which counts datasets rather than reporting a metric. Approximations that do carry a printed digit are counted ('~50ms', '~0.5 mIoU', 'an estimated 4%'), unlike the worked example's digit-free 'around half'. Much of this paper's evidence is in figures that print nothing: Figures 5, 6, 7, 9b, 9c, 9d, 10, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 19 and 20 carry only axis-tick calibration, legend text, method names or qualitative image panels, so every one of them counts 0, exactly as in the worked example. The three exceptions are Figure 9a, whose bars are labelled with their values, and Figures 11 and 18, whose legends print rating means. random.seed(20260810); random.sample(range(1, 160), 15) drew {1, 2, 13, 14, 25, 29, 70, 83, 91, 99, 107, 108, 122, 148, 153}; each label below records its draw as frame_index. Three draws (1, 2, 99) are prose values with no row or column to attribute and needed no image. The other twelve land on five pages, and exactly those five were rendered as page images to attribute each value to the right row and column: page 8 (Table 2; draws 13, 14, 25, 29), page 10 (Table 4; draw 70), page 11 (Table 5; draws 83, 91), page 19 (Table 6; draws 107, 108) and page 24 (Figure 18 and Table 8; draws 122, 148, 153). No other page was rendered; the frame itself was enumerated from the page text. The page images also corrected one ordering assumption: the text dump lists each Figure 18 legend as RITM, SAM - single output, SAM, GT, whereas the legend is printed in two columns and reads RITM, SAM, SAM - single output, GT. The printed order is the one used for indexing; draw 122 is the first entry of panel (c) either way.

Mask AP for the fully-supervised baseline. Recorded unconfident because ownership is genuinely unclear rather than because the transcription is: the row carries the citation [62], which by the usual rule makes it a quoted baseline, but Appendix D.4 states the authors ran 'a fully-supervised ViTDet-H on COCO and LVIS v1 validation splits' to produce the box prompts for SAM, and Appendix E states they rated ViTDet-H's masks in their own human study, so this AP may equally be their own measurement of that run -- which would make it an own result under the rerun rule. 'We therefore tested a fourth setup that uses only the automatically generated masks. With this data, SAM performs only marginally lower than using all data (~0.5 mIoU).' It counts because no absolute is printed beside it or anywhere else -- Figure 13 (left), which plots this comparison, prints only the axis ticks 50/60/70. Printed in the panel legend as '5.9 +/- 0.14, RITM'; the mean of 1000 annotator ratings on a 1-10 scale, with a 95% confidence interval that is not a separate cell. The mask being rated is RITM's [92], a baseline model, but the number is the authors' own measurement -- Appendix E describes their human study, their annotators and their rubric -- so ownership is theirs per the rule that ownership is per cell and a caption may claim the measurement while the method stays quoted. Printed as '2e-57'. The paired t-test that SAM's mean mask quality rating exceeds RITM's on IBD, from the authors' own human study; the caption states 'P-values are calculated by paired t-test'. Recorded as role result because it is a number the paper reports as an outcome of its own experiment and neither hyperparameter nor dataset_statistic fits; a reviewer who holds that a significance test is not a claim about performance would drop this cell and the other 14 p-values, taking N from 159 to 144. The CI99 column beside it, '(1.03, 1.39)', is an interval and is deliberately not a cell. Row and column verified against the page image.

Printed as '3e-10'. The second of the two hypotheses tested per row -- that SAM outranks its own ablated single-output variant -- so both models in this comparison are the authors'. Same role reading as frame_index 148. OVIS is the one panel of Figure 18 where SAM's mean (7.2) is below single-output SAM's (7.7), which makes this row worth a careful read: the p-value is nonetheless printed in the 'SAM > SAM single out.' column with CI99 (0.27, 0.63), and the caption asserts all intervals exclude zero. Transcribed as printed from the page image without attempting to reconcile that tension, which is the paper's to explain.
